findings.title: shirudo: BPF live-patching infra for the agentic era
findings.summary_md: At the Linux Plumbers Conference in Prague, Isovalent engineers Daniel Borkmann and John Fastabend presented Shirudo as an agentless BPF live-patching platform for production fleets, Kubernetes nodes and air-gapped devices. The talk says the project deliberately avoids a config DSL because agents work directly in code, and that it uses extended attributes, signed BPF programs and BPF LSM seals to resist tampering by untrusted root. The session covered the operator and target workflow, architecture internals, a demo and gaps on the BPF kernel and loader side.

findings.title: PHP2Shell: A tale of two PHP remote vulnerabilities
findings.summary_md: Calif Research disclosed PHP2Shell, two remote code execution flaws tracked as CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619, with OpenAI and Wiz in the PHP October 2026 security release. The write-up says the earliest affected path goes back to PHP 5.4.0 and demonstrated pre-auth RCE against WordPress 7.1.2, Drupal 11.4.3, Joomla 6.1.4, MediaWiki 1.46.2 and Magento 2.4.9 in default configurations. It links the bugs to memory-limit fatal errors that interrupt native code before cleanup and leave dangling state.

findings.title: Critical Java Vulnerability Requires Immediate Patching
findings.summary_md: CISA urged immediate patching of CVE-2026-114938, a critical memory corruption flaw in the Base64 decoder of the x86-64 HotSpot JVM that can crash the JVM and permit unauthenticated remote code execution. The alert tells organizations to inventory JDKs bundled with third-party applications, container images and appliances, and to prioritize internet-facing systems. Where patching is not immediately feasible, CISA recommends validating and restricting Base64 input at the application boundary, setting input-size limits and limiting unauthenticated access; it also calls for hunting rogue runtimes, unexpected JVM crashes and suspicious Java processes.

findings.title: Java4Shell: Write once, RCE everywhere
findings.summary_md: Calif disclosed CVE-2026-114938 in the x86-64 Base64 intrinsic of OpenJDK HotSpot, scoring it 9.2 under CVSS 4.0, and described malformed input that underflows a store mask and writes 64 bytes into a 50-byte decoded buffer. The researcher demonstrated pre-auth RCE in Keycloak, Jira, Confluence, Artifactory, Jenkins and PingFederate, and post-auth RCE in Kafka, Solr, Elasticsearch, Gerrit and Spinnaker. The write-up also covers JavaBleed heap disclosure, a client-side path through a malicious TLS server, and startup flags that avoid the faulty intrinsic.

findings.title: Java4Shell (CVE-2026-114938): Frequently asked questions about OpenJDK RCE vulnerability
findings.summary_md: Tenable records that Oracle released Java4Shell fixes on November 17 and lists fixed builds 17.0.21.1, 21.0.13.1, 25.0.5.1 and 27.0.1.1 for Oracle and Temurin, plus 8u513-perf for the Java 8 Enterprise Performance Pack. It says exploitation requires x86-64 CPUs with AVX-512 VBMI and an application that passes untrusted data to the affected Base64 APIs, which excludes ARM64 and limits the set of reachable applications. As of November 18 GreyNoise had reported attempts but no confirmed successful exploitation, and CVE-2026-114938 was not listed in CISA's KEV catalog.

findings.title: The First Java4Shell Attack Attempts Are Here: GreyNoise Logs 187 Booby-Trapped Login Headers, Cloudflare Sees Scanners Return Disguised as Chrome, and SOC Tools Are on the Affected Lists
findings.summary_md: SOCtember reports that GreyNoise's tracking page, updated at 10:48 UTC on November 19, recorded 187 Java4Shell-shaped requests from five IP addresses with no confirmed intrusions. GreyNoise defines an attempt as an HTTP Authorization Basic or Bearer value of 64 or 128 characters plus one to three more ending in an equals sign; the busiest source requested Confluence paths and a Spring Boot actuator endpoint. Cloudforce One saw a scanner return about 17 hours later posing as Chrome, and the article advises hunting Authorization values of 65 to 67 or 129 to 131 characters ending in an equals sign at reverse proxies, load balancers and WAFs.

findings.title: OpenAI and Cisco introduce Shirudo
findings.summary_md: OpenAI and Cisco announced Shirudo as an open-source runtime for protecting running Linux systems while patches are tested and rolled out. The post describes four capabilities: live eBPF shields with pre-enforcement monitoring, programmable agent controls, cryptographically signed and verified shields, and TPM-backed records of protections being loaded or removed. In a controlled test, a Codex-generated shield added an input check to Java's Base64 decoder and blocked a Java4Shell attempt against a running Elasticsearch service without a restart; the runtime is BSD 2-Clause with BPF programs dual-licensed under BSD and GPL.

findings.title: Cisco and OpenAI Launch Shirudo, A New Project to Safeguard Agentic AI
findings.summary_md: Cisco and OpenAI launched Shirudo on November 23, 2026 as an open-source eBPF project for running Linux hosts, with shields signed so the host can verify them before loading even if an attacker has administrator access. The press release says agents can find a vulnerability, build a shield and test that it stops the attack without disrupting the service, and that the project wrote code blocking both Java4Shell and a recent PHP flaw. It frames the effort as a move from human-paced policy updates to agent-driven defense while people keep deployment control.

findings.title: Cisco and OpenAI introduce Shirudo
findings.summary_md: Isovalent's technical post says Shirudo is a rewrite of Tetragon that lets agents write code instead of working through a policy language designed for humans. It describes a one-shot CLI, an eBPF control plane loaded into the kernel at boot, signed .bee packages delivered through an OCI registry and validated on targets using TPMs, and a shield hit count that represents exploitation attempts. The Java4Shell example added Java bytecode validation on the Base64 decoder of Elasticsearch 9.5.5; log lines show `Base64 guard installed on java.util.Base64$Decoder.decode0 (classfile)` and `Base64 guard rejected candidate: length=65, padding=1, remainder=1, alphabet=standard`.

findings.title: Expanding the Defender's Window with Self-defending Infrastructure
findings.summary_md: Cisco's Jeetu Patel says AI found the recent PHP flaw and Java bug through a startup using the OpenAI Cyber model, and that exploit campaigns for both were underway within a day of disclosure, if not before. The post says the PHP vulnerability was reported to affect an estimated 70 percent of global websites and web infrastructure, and argues that the defender's window is shrinking from days to minutes and hours. It describes Shirudo shields as moving to active blocking only when evidence shows they are safe and retiring when the real patch lands.

findings.title: Cisco and OpenAI pitch eBPF kernel plugins as the way to tame the patchpocalypse
findings.summary_md: The Register covered the launch on November 24, 2026, framing Shirudo as an open-source compensating control built on eBPF programs that run sandboxed in the kernel. It notes Cisco and OpenAI expect humans to check every generated shield before production use, and that the demonstrated Java mitigation blocked the recent flaw without downtime for Elasticsearch. The article sets the project against more than 100,000 software flaws reported that year and notes the commercial interest for Codex and Cisco's Isovalent unit.
